method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across visible belief, words made deeds, widening care for strangers and opponents, trust in dealings and public service, humility and self-examination, steadfastness under trial, the inward sources of love, prayer and the Covenant, particular people and communities, families, education and the life of women, and a life that leaves light in the world. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: He whose deeds do not accord with his words is not a true Baha'i.
selected.reason: Reported saying that one whose deeds do not accord with his words is not a true Bahá’í; the guide’s plainest test of practice.

selected.text: Our actions reveal what we are, no matter what the tongue speaks.
selected.reason: Reported saying that our actions reveal what we are whatever the tongue speaks; a terse, memorable form of the guide’s test of practice.

selected.text: Let the world profit by your teachings and learn from your examples!
selected.reason: Reported exhortation that the world profit from believers’ teachings and learn from their examples; joins teaching to example.

selected.text: A true Baha'i is one who acts in accordance with the blessed teachings.
selected.reason: Reported definition of a true Bahá’í as one who acts in accordance with the teachings, spoken in Stuttgart; a plain statement of the subject’s core.

selected.text: Aid the Cause of God through the hosts of goodly character and refined conduct.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s short counsel to aid the Cause through the hosts of goodly character and refined conduct; a concise practical form of the hosts image.

selected.text: Therefore my intention is that he should know that the Baha'is are faithful and appreciative.
selected.reason: Tablet stating the intention that a person should know the Bahá’ís are faithful and appreciative; supplies the gratitude named in this section.

selected.text: the loved ones must adopt a manner and conduct that attracts hearts, not causes souls to flee
selected.reason: Tablet asking the loved ones to adopt a manner that attracts hearts rather than causing souls to flee; a brief practical test of conduct toward others.

selected.text: he hath no thoughts of self, is self-effacing in the Cause, possesseth a pure heart and a radiant soul
selected.reason: Tablet describing a believer with no thoughts of self, self-effacing in the Cause; a brief portrait of humility.

selected.text: These are the attributes of the Baha'is. Otherwise, what use is there in being a Baha'i in word alone.
selected.reason: Reported question “what use is there in being a Baha'i in word alone”; a brief but pointed test of names.

selected.text: The duty of the believers of God is to be the servants to each other and attend to each otheris wants
selected.reason: Reported words that the duty of believers is to be servants to each other and attend to each other’s wants; a plain statement of mutual service.

selected.text: Today, the sign and proof of every true Baha'i are deeds and actions that conform to the divine teachings
selected.reason: Tablet naming deeds and actions that conform to the divine teachings as the sign and proof of every true Bahá’í; a direct definition of the visible sign.

selected.text: Thou harbourest no ill-will or animosity toward anyone. With all thou art pleasant, sincere, loving and kind.
selected.reason: Tablet praising one who harbours no ill will toward anyone and is pleasant and kind to all; a concise example of goodwill.

selected.text: Forbearance in the face of anger is among the characteristics of the righteous and the qualities of the noble
selected.reason: Tablet naming forbearance in the face of anger as a mark of the righteous; a concise statement of self-restraint.

selected.text: So if the believers wish for my happiness, they must adorn themselves with heavenly character and conduct
selected.reason: Reported words that believers who wish for ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s happiness must adorn themselves with heavenly character and conduct; a personal appeal.

selected.text: This man is not a Bahai in a normal way, but in a real manner; he is a Bahai in deed and not in words alone
selected.reason: Reported remark on a man who is a Bahá’í “in deed and not in words alone”; a brief narrative example of the test of practice.

selected.text: She was one of the best teachers of the Cause. An eloquent tongue, a severed soul, a detached heart were hers.
selected.reason: Tablet remembering a woman as one of the best teachers of the Cause, with an eloquent tongue and detached heart; a named example of women’s service.

selected.text: Baha'i emblem. It is wondrously well done! Yet the badge of the Baha'is must be such conduct, deeds, and manners as are in conformity with the teachings of Baha'u'llah
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: This prisoner is grateful and pleased with the manner and conduct of those divine friends, the Persian loved ones
selected.reason: Tablet in which the prisoner ‘Abdu’l-Bahá expresses gratitude for the conduct of the Persian loved ones; a community remembered.

selected.text: We have adorned the heaven of man with the stars of steadfastness, trustworthiness, truthfulness and faithfulness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the heaven of man adorned with the stars of steadfastness, trustworthiness, truthfulness and faithfulness; a memorable image of character.

selected.text: praise be to God, the friends of Khuy possess spiritual character and nature, and radiant faces and merciful hearts
selected.reason: Tablet praising the friends of Khuy for spiritual character, radiant faces and merciful hearts; remembers a particular community.

selected.text: As for the friends in Kirman, they are full of spirit and joy, and are self-sacrificing in service to the Threshold
selected.reason: Tablet reporting that the friends in Kirman are full of spirit and self-sacrificing in service; remembers a particular community.

selected.text: In short a Baha'i is a remedy for every ailment, a balm for every wound and a consolation for every despondent heart.
selected.reason: Reported description of a Bahá’í as a remedy for every ailment and a balm for every wound; a memorable image of service.

selected.text: The loved ones of God must be such that from them the fragrance of musk is diffused, not the foul odor of ungodliness.
selected.reason: Reported words that the loved ones must diffuse the fragrance of musk, not the foul odour of ungodliness; a memorable image.

selected.text: The sign of faithfulness to Baha'u'llah is that precious souls arise with sacred breaths to serve at the Holy Threshold.
selected.reason: Tablet stating that the sign of faithfulness to Bahá’u’lláh is arising to serve at the Threshold; a concise test of faithfulness.

selected.text: Be ye dawning-places of faithfulness amidst the concourse of creation and daysprings of trustworthiness among the servants.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to be dawning-places of faithfulness and daysprings of trustworthiness; a concise authoritative call to trustworthiness.

selected.text: You must associate with the handmaidens of God in perfect joy and fragrance, chastity and purity, certitude and detachment.
selected.reason: Tablet asking a believer to associate with the handmaidens of God in joy, chastity and detachment; touches the life of women.

selected.text: Be a lamp, the light of which may dispel the darkness, and a real standard which may remove the doubts of the veiled people.
selected.reason: Tablet bidding a believer be a lamp that dispels darkness and a standard that removes doubts; a concise call to example.

selected.text: the heaven of the station of the handmaidens of God hath been and shall ever be illumined by one luminary, and that is chastity
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that the heaven of the handmaidens’ station is illumined by one luminary, chastity; a concise authoritative statement.

selected.text: There are so many people who let the opportunity slip and of their hands on account of the slowness of their minds and bodies.
selected.reason: Reported warning that many let opportunity slip through slowness of mind and body; supplies the punctuality theme named in this section.

selected.text: We love to behold you as horizons of light unto the inhabitants of all lands and as daysprings of mercy unto all created things.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s wish to behold believers as horizons of light and daysprings of mercy to all created things; a brief closing statement of mercy.

selected.text: The loved ones of Nayriz are intoxicated with the choice wine of faithfulness from an elegant cup of steadfastness and loyalty.
selected.reason: Tablet describing the loved ones of Nayríz as intoxicated with the wine of faithfulness and steadfastness; remembers a particular persecuted community.

selected.text: the divine friends in these severe days will … manifest such strength of heart that all the people of the world will be astonished
selected.reason: Tablet hoping the divine friends in severe days show such strength of heart that the world is astonished; supports the theme of steadfastness under trial.

selected.text: You must in every case show patience and forbearance and, considering the divine counsels, demonstrate tolerance and good conduct.
selected.reason: Tablet counselling patience, forbearance and tolerance in every case in light of the divine counsels; a practical rule for difficult situations.

selected.text: All of you may help each other and be ever ready to sacrifice your lives for each other. This is the quality of the people of Baha.
selected.reason: Tablet asking believers to help one another and be ready to sacrifice their lives for each other; a brief statement of mutual devotion.

selected.text: But the friends must acquire the characteristics of the Daystar of the horizons and promote and teach more through deeds than words.
selected.reason: Tablet urging the friends to teach more through deeds than words; a concise practical application of the subject.

selected.text: Be thou loving, good natured and fragrant in thy fellowship. Be radiant, cheerful and full of sympathy towards the peoples of the earth
selected.reason: Tablet bidding the believer be loving, fragrant in fellowship, radiant and cheerful toward the peoples of the earth; a brief portrait of everyday warmth.

selected.text: The friends of God must, God willing, manifest such deeds and character that all may inhale from them the fragrance of the love of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s wish that the friends show such deeds and character that all inhale from them the fragrance of the love of God; supports the guide’s fragrance imagery.

selected.text: that the seekers may take thee as a model of guidance and thou mayest be for them a goodly example in the fear of God and righteousness
selected.reason: Tablet hoping a believer becomes a model for seekers and a goodly example in the fear of God and righteousness; states the role of example for those who are searching.

selected.text: He commits no violence; if he is struck he does not return the blow. He calls nothing bad, following the example of the Lord Baha'u'llah.
selected.reason: Reported words that a believer commits no violence, does not return a blow and calls nothing bad; a clear statement of non-retaliation.

selected.text: These are the manifestations of detachment and the dawning-places of the fear of God. Upon them rest God's peace, His grace and His favor.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on the manifestations of detachment and dawning-places of the fear of God; names the fear of God among the inward sources.

selected.text: the Afnans of this blessed Tree must, God willing, yield such fruits as to become the manifestation of "By their fruits ye shall know them."
selected.reason: Tablet asking the Afnán to yield fruits that fulfil “By their fruits ye shall know them”; ties the tree image to a particular family.

selected.text: The insincere man learns from him the lessons of sincerity, the faithless becomes faithful, the ignorant wise, and the cowardly, courageous.
selected.reason: Reported description of a sincere believer from whom the insincere learn sincerity and the cowardly courage; shows the transforming influence of example.

selected.text: My hope is that every one of the believers may become a brilliant jewel of the mine of guidance and a shining star of the heaven of virtue.
selected.reason: Reported hope that every believer become a brilliant jewel of the mine of guidance and a shining star of the heaven of virtue; a closing hope for growth.

selected.text: We counsel all to perform pure and holy deeds. Some among the Babis have grown exceedingly indolent. They must hold fast unto the Law of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling pure and holy deeds and noting that some Bábís have grown indolent; a candid historical qualification that profession is not enough.

selected.text: those who are steadfast are like trees that have strong roots and foundations. Storms cannot shake them; rather, they add to their freshness
selected.reason: Reported image of the steadfast as trees with strong roots whom storms cannot shake but only freshen; opens the theme of steadfastness under trial.

selected.text: if noble blood is joined with a goodly character, meaning if the son walks in the steps of the father, then the relationship of sonship is real
selected.reason: Tablet stating that sonship is real when noble blood is joined with goodly character and the son walks in the father’s steps; a distinctive statement on family.

selected.text: The followers of the Blessed Perfection are the invincible army of Peace and are showing by their deeds and words that they are the peace-makers.
selected.reason: Reported description of the followers of Bahá’u’lláh as an invincible army of peace who show by deeds and words that they are peace-makers; a memorable image of peace.

selected.text: You are a kindly friend to the friends … like the morning breeze, are light in spirit, and like the gentle air, are the cause of joy and gladness
selected.reason: Tablet praising a kindly friend who is like the morning breeze, the cause of joy and gladness; a personal example of warmth.

selected.text: Let your acts be a guide unto all mankind, that from your behaviour and conduct they may be enabled to recognize the signs and commandments of God.
selected.reason: Words of Bahá’u’lláh asking that believers’ acts guide mankind to recognize the signs of God; states the purpose of visible conduct.

selected.text: strive with utmost endeavor so that you may attract the ancient Parsees through deeds and conduct and speech and goodly character and refined manners.
selected.reason: Tablet urging the friends to attract the ancient Parsees through deeds, conduct and refined manners; a distinctive application of example to a particular community.

selected.text: One might say, 'Well, I will endure such-and-such a person so long as he is endurable.' But Baha'is must endure people even when they are unendurable.
selected.reason: Reported saying that Bahá’ís must endure people even when they are unendurable; the guide’s memorable statement on patience with a difficult companion.

selected.text: Thank the Lord that thou art born of a father who is pure and a mother who is chaste and that thou hast been raised in the cradle of belief and certitude
selected.reason: Tablet bidding a believer thank God for a pure father, a chaste mother and a cradle of belief; recognizes the family as a setting of faith.

selected.text: The best man is that person who cheers and gladdens the broken-hearted ones and the worst man is that soul who causes suffering and pain to one's heart.
selected.reason: Reported saying that the best person gladdens the broken-hearted and the worst causes pain to a heart; a memorable measure of conduct.

selected.text: They should witness such perfections among the loved ones of God, observe such conduct and behavior, that they are compelled to submission and humility.
selected.reason: Reported wish that people witness such perfections in the loved ones that they are moved to submission and humility; shows conduct as persuasion without argument.

selected.text: They must live and conduct themselves in such manner that in sanctity, prayerfulness and devotion they may become distinguished from the rest of mankind.
selected.reason: Tablet asking believers to be distinguished in sanctity, prayerfulness and devotion; names prayer among the sources of conduct.

selected.text: When finally we hasten from this world to the next, we should do so with a candle in our hand, a brightness in our countenance, and a spirit in our heart.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: We counsel thee and My loved ones to trustworthiness and truthfulness and purity, and to that whereby the station of man is made manifest among the peoples.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling trustworthiness, truthfulness and purity and that whereby the station of man is made manifest; ties these virtues to human dignity.

selected.text: The more thou showest humility before these brilliant stars and shining orbs, the more will thy power of fatherhood increase and thy paternal authority grow.
selected.reason: Tablet telling a father that the more humility he shows his children the more his paternal authority grows; a distinctive application of humility to family.

selected.text: We counsel you to be trustworthy, religious, chaste and faithful, and to that whereby the Cause of God, the Lord of all that was and shall be, may be exalted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling believers to be trustworthy, religious, chaste and faithful so that the Cause may be exalted; an authoritative list of core virtues.

selected.text: The companions of the Crimson Ark must distinguish themselves among the people of the world in such wise that all may testify to their detachment and holiness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call that the companions of the Crimson Ark be distinguished so that all testify to their detachment and holiness; joins steadfastness to visible conduct.

selected.text: Today the people of Baha are souls who should become renowned throughout all regions for possessing the character, conduct and behavior of the Supreme Concourse
selected.reason: Tablet hoping the people of Bahá become renowned in all regions for the conduct of the Supreme Concourse; links reputation to heavenly character.

selected.text: Praise be to God, he is adorned with the ornament of love and crowned with the diadem of steadfastness. We bear witness to his recognition, love and precedence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s testimony that a believer is adorned with love and crowned with the diadem of steadfastness; a remembrance of a particular person.

selected.text: meek and lowly for the sake of God among His beloved, denying self and passion, grasping the robe of piety, so that they may be lamps of guidance in those regions.
selected.reason: Tablet asking believers to be meek and lowly among the beloved, denying self and passion, as lamps of guidance; joins humility to service.

selected.text: Thus those who claim attachment to the Truth must surely manifest signs of sanctity in their deeds and the radiance of joy must be witnessed in their countenances.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that those claiming attachment to the Truth must show sanctity in deeds and radiant joy in their faces; adds joy to the signs of faith.

selected.text: O people of God! You must manifest yourselves in such wise that no opportunity remains for the barking ones - that is, their hopes may be transformed into despair.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to the people of God to conduct themselves so that no opportunity remains for “the barking ones”; conduct as the answer to detractors.

selected.text: Regard faith as a tree: its fruits and leaves, its branches and boughs are, and ever have been, truthfulness, trustworthiness, rectitude of conduct, and forbearance.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Verily, I say unto you: none will be saved but the believers, and from the believers only the sincere, and even those are in great danger, especially in such a time.
selected.reason: Tablet warning that none will be saved but the believers, and of them only the sincere, who are themselves in danger; the guide’s severe warning against complacency.

selected.text: Today bravery and manliness, courage and valor and wisdom are trustworthiness. Trustworthiness is religiosity. Religiosity is truthfulness. Truthfulness is steadfastness.
selected.reason: Tablet equating bravery and wisdom with trustworthiness, religiosity, truthfulness and steadfastness; a compact chain of the virtues that define a believer.

selected.text: Those souls who are of the Kingdom eagerly wish to be of service to the poor, to sympathize with them, to show kindness to the miserable and to make their lives fruitful.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: they must strive with utmost honesty, purity, truthfulness, chastity and steadfastness in carrying out their assigned duties … This is the way and conduct of the Baha'is
selected.reason: Tablet requiring utmost honesty, purity and steadfastness in carrying out assigned duties as the way of the Bahá’ís; applies the subject to public service.

selected.text: He was set ablaze with the fire of Your love among humanity and called others to Your remembrance with a radiant countenance and a heart drawn to Your Most Exalted Beauty
selected.reason: Prayer remembering a believer set ablaze with the love of God who called others to remembrance with a radiant countenance; a remembrance of a particular life.

selected.text: Thus you know neither opposition, dislike, nor hatred, for every living creature is dear to you and the good of each is sought. … These are perfect human sentiments and virtues
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O kind friend! At this moment I thought of you and became very happy, for your character and disposition and the radiance of your countenance became embodied before 'Abdu'l-Baha.
selected.reason: Letter in which ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls a kind friend whose character and radiant face became present before Him; a personal remembrance.

selected.text: His honor Aqa Mirza Muhammad-Baqir Khan is truly firm in the Covenant and a helper of the oppressed and a succorer of the helpless. In whatever he can do he shows no shortcoming.
selected.reason: Tablet commending Mírzá Muhammad-Báqir Khán as firm in the Covenant and a helper of the oppressed; a named example of service.

selected.text: They should be kind to all people and prefer the welfare of others to their own … consider his characteristics, his sincerity, truthfulness, willingness to serve, trustworthiness
selected.reason: Reported counsel to prefer the welfare of others and to judge a person by sincerity, truthfulness, willingness to serve and trustworthiness; a practical standard for regarding others.

selected.text: O people of God! The victorious hosts today are praiseworthy character and deeds. We have enjoined upon Our loved ones goodly conduct and the fear of God, the Lord of all worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s address to the people of God naming praiseworthy character and deeds as the victorious hosts of today; an authoritative restatement of the hosts image.

selected.text: The servants of the Blessed Beauty must be thus - from their countenance a manifest light radiates, and from their conduct and speech the signs of nobility are evident and apparent.
selected.reason: Tablet stating that from the servants of the Blessed Beauty a light radiates and signs of nobility appear in conduct and speech; a clear standard.

selected.text: I ask God that the spiritual assembly of Philadelphia may become the gathering-place of the Merciful One, and the believers become the embodiment of the qualities of heavenly angels.
selected.reason: Tablet praying that the spiritual assembly of Philadelphia become a gathering-place of the Merciful and its believers embody angelic qualities; applies the subject to a community.

selected.text: God willing, the friends of Truth must appear among the servants with perfect trustworthiness, truthfulness and praiseworthy character. They are as lamps amid the darkness of the age.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that the friends must appear with perfect trustworthiness and truthfulness as lamps amid the darkness of the age; a memorable image of integrity.

selected.text: Be distinguished among the servants from all others, such that thy countenance shineth amidst all faces, and be among those whose faces are illumined by the lights of the Countenance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to be distinguished among the servants so that one’s countenance shines among all faces; supports the closing call to distinction.

selected.text: And the glory be upon thee and upon the handmaidens of God who are steadfast in the Cause, pure from defilement, preserved from uncleanliness, and have attained unto the command of God
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s blessing on the handmaidens who are steadfast in the Cause and pure from defilement; an authoritative tribute to women.

selected.text: Today the people of Baha are souls whom tales have not debarred from the holy Kingdom of God. They behold His signs with their own eyes and hearken with their own ears unto His verses.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that the people of Bahá are those whom tales have not debarred and who behold His signs with their own eyes; adds independent seeing to steadfastness.

selected.text: A person whose tree of life produces such fruits is a Baha'i: otherwise he is of the earth earthly, self-occupied and following the dictates of his own desire and is 'man' only by name.
selected.reason: Reported words that one whose tree of life yields such fruits is a Bahá’í, while another is “man” only by name; reinforces the tree image and the limits of names.

selected.text: friends might be raised up who would be as firm and steadfast as immovable mountains in their constancy and steadfastness, and like the spirit of life itself in their character and deeds
selected.reason: Tablet hoping friends arise as firm as immovable mountains and like the spirit of life itself in character and deeds; joins steadfastness to life-giving conduct.

selected.text: The loved ones of God must conduct themselves with such steadfastness and composure that all beings will be astonished at what constancy and firmness, what dignity and composure this is.
selected.reason: Tablet asking the loved ones to show such steadfastness and composure that all beings are astonished; a direct call to firmness.

selected.text: These are the souls whose mention was revealed aforetime in the Perspicuous Book - His exalted Word: "honored servants who speak not until He hath spoken, and who do as they are bidden."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing souls as “honored servants who speak not until He hath spoken, and who do as they are bidden”; a scriptural image of obedience.

selected.text: Their faces are radiant and their hearts are gardens of the flowers of knowledge. Their eyes are open to the Kingdom of mystery and their souls are intimate and harmonious with each other.
selected.reason: Tablet describing believers whose hearts are gardens of knowledge and whose souls are harmonious with one another; joins inward life to fellowship.

selected.text: The people of Baha must be manifestations of the greatest chastity and supreme virtue … The meaning is that purity and sanctity are among the greatest characteristics of the people of Baha
selected.reason: Tablet naming chastity and purity as among the greatest characteristics of the people of Bahá; adds chastity to the guide’s list of virtues.

selected.text: Surely like him you will arise with such conduct and behavior as will be the cause of eternal glory and everlasting life, so that pure soul may become joyous and glad in the luminous realm.
selected.reason: Tablet hoping a bereaved believer will arise with conduct like the departed so that his pure soul may rejoice; a remembrance that turns into example.

selected.text: As far as thou art able, show kindness unto all people, manifest love, and follow the path of friendship, truthfulness and reconciliation, that thou mayest become the very soul of the friends
selected.reason: Tablet urging kindness to all, love, truthfulness and reconciliation so that the believer becomes the very soul of the friends; a compact counsel of friendship.

selected.text: Thus the Baha'is must live such a perfect life among men, that even those who will not see this Truth or believe in it, would not fail to be impressed by the noble life they live as Baha'is.
selected.reason: Reported counsel that Bahá’ís live so noble a life that even those who never accept the Truth are impressed; supports the guide’s concern with conduct that does not depend on conversion.

selected.text: For the opposition of the world did not hinder them, nor did the might of rulers weaken them. They appear with complete power. Upon them be the glory of God and the lights of His mighty throne.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s tribute to those whom the opposition of the world and the might of rulers did not hinder; supports the theme of steadfastness under pressure.

selected.text: By these things you know the faithful servant of God. How do we know the light? By its rays. So when you see these qualities, you will know that the servant of God has received the regeneration
selected.reason: Reported comparison of knowing the faithful servant by his qualities as light is known by its rays; a clear image of faith recognized through its effects.

selected.text: Each one of you must be even as the morning star, radiant, that souls who have strayed in the darkness of idle fancies and selfish desires may thereby be guided and find the path of deliverance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to be radiant as the morning star so that souls strayed in darkness may find deliverance; states the purpose of distinction as help to others.

selected.text: I consider him [Tolstoy] a Baha'i, a real Baha'i, because he lived and acted in accord with the good-pleasure of Baha'u'llah, because he divided all his estate between himself and his farmers
selected.reason: Reported remark calling Tolstoy a real Bahá’í because he lived in accord with Bahá’u’lláh’s good-pleasure and divided his estate with his farmers; a distinctive narrative example.

selected.text: Adorn your tongues with truthfulness, and your hands with generosity, and your bodies with dignity, and your souls with courtesy, and your hearts with My love and then with My exalted remembrance
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to adorn tongues with truthfulness, hands with generosity, bodies with dignity and hearts with His love; a memorable summary of the whole person.

selected.text: O people of Baha! Hearken unto My call. It behooveth you to counsel the servants through your deeds and character. Verily He is with you, seeing and hearing, and He is the Mighty, the All-Seeing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s call to the people of Bahá to counsel the servants through their deeds and character, for He is seeing and hearing; a concise authoritative summary.

selected.text: These are the companions of the Crimson Ark. By the life of God! All divine Books and Scriptures bear witness to the greatness of this Cause and to the excellence and nobility of these companions.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that all Scriptures bear witness to the nobility of the companions of the Crimson Ark; introduces the Crimson Ark imagery.

selected.text: With every group, even if it be an oppressive party, they must act with the utmost trustworthiness, religiosity and kindness. This is the path of the Baha'is, this is the way of the spiritual ones.
selected.reason: Tablet requiring trustworthiness and kindness even toward an oppressive party; a necessary extension of kindness to opponents.

selected.text: Every soul that hath today drunk from the living waters and turned toward the Most Exalted Horizon must needs walk among the servants in such wise that all will testify to his sanctity and detachment.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words that every soul who has drunk the living waters must walk among people so that all testify to his sanctity; joins inward faith to visible conduct.

selected.text: Be good-natured and cheerful, sweet-scented and attractive, truthful in speech - these are the requirements of kindness. … Be as a son to the elderly, a father to the youth, and a brother to your peers
selected.reason: Tablet naming cheerfulness and truthful speech as requirements of kindness and asking one to be a son to the elderly, a father to the youth and a brother to peers; a distinctive practical image.

selected.text: He was a warm person, full of enthusiasm, never cold or indifferent. He went through much trouble for the friends … Steadfast, firm, believing, assured - what else is the fruit of human life but this
selected.reason: Reported remembrance of a warm, enthusiastic believer who took trouble for the friends, asking “what else is the fruit of human life but this”; a personal example.

selected.text: If a man considers himself humble and lowly in the Cause of God, he becomes glorified in all eyes. On the other hand, the moment he aspires to personal greatness, he falls into disgrace and oblivion
selected.reason: Reported saying that one who considers himself lowly is glorified while one who aspires to greatness falls into oblivion; a clear statement of humility.

selected.text: Ye must shine with such a delicacy, such tenderness, and such a noble magnanimity that ye shall verily become the highest ornaments in this divine garden, the crowning glory of the true meadow of heaven
